title: Lesson 1: Introduction to IT in Business
subject: IT Application Tools in Business
description: Learn how information technology supports business operations and modern accountancy.
learningObjectives: Define information technology and identify its six core components
Explain how IT supports business operations, communication, decisions, competitiveness, and security
Describe how IT improves transaction recording, reporting, auditing, taxation, analysis, accuracy, and compliance in accountancy
Identify common business and accounting-specific IT tools

pages.title: Definition of IT
pages.content:
Information Technology (IT) refers to the use of computers, software, networks, and other electronic systems to collect, process, store, protect, and share information.

IT includes hardware such as computers, servers, and networking devices, as well as software such as applications, databases, and accounting systems. Together, these resources help individuals and organizations manage data and make better decisions.

Key idea: IT is not only computers. It is a complete system of technology, information, people, and procedures.

pages.title: Components of Information Technology
pages.content:
Six connected components allow an information system to work effectively.

ComponentMeaningExamples
HardwarePhysical parts of a computer systemComputers, servers, keyboards, printers, storage devices
SoftwarePrograms that tell hardware what to doExcel, QuickBooks, SAP, accounting systems
DataRaw facts processed into useful informationSales numbers, financial records, customer lists
PeopleUsers who perform tasks and make decisionsAccountants, auditors, managers, IT staff
ProcessesRules and procedures for using ITEntering, processing, storing, and reporting financial data
Networks and communicationSystems that connect computers and share informationInternet, intranets, Wi-Fi, cloud computing

pages.title: Role of IT in Business
pages.content:
IT has become a backbone of modern business and supports organizations in almost every area.

Automation of processes
Reduces manual work and speeds up operations, such as automated payroll and online banking.
Efficient communication
Connects departments and clients through email, messaging, video conferencing, and collaboration tools.
Data storage and management
Stores and organizes large amounts of information, including company files and financial records.
Decision-making support
Provides timely reports and dashboards, such as profit and loss trends.
Competitive advantage
Supports digital marketing, e-commerce, online customer service, and innovation.
Security of information
Protects sensitive information through controls such as encryption and access restrictions.

pages.title: Role of IT in Accountancy
pages.content:
For accountants, IT is essential to modern practice because it makes financial processes faster, more accurate, and more reliable.

Recording transactions
Systems can automatically enter and classify sales, expenses, and payroll transactions.
Financial reporting
Accounting software can generate balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements.
Auditing and assurance
Audit tools such as ACL or IDEA help identify errors, unusual patterns, and possible fraud.
Taxation
Electronic tools simplify tax computation and filing, including eBIR forms in the Philippines.
Data analysis and decision-making
Tools such as Excel pivot tables help accountants analyze expenses and support business strategy.
Accuracy and error reduction
Automated formulas reduce mistakes caused by repeated manual calculations.
Compliance and regulations
Enterprise systems help organizations track requirements under standards such as GAAP or IFRS.

pages.title: General Business IT Tools
pages.content:
Businesses use different tools for documents, analysis, communication, data storage, and security.

  • Microsoft Office: Word for reports, Excel for analysis and computations, and PowerPoint for presentations.
  • Email and communication: Outlook, Gmail, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Slack.
  • Databases: Microsoft Access, MySQL, and Oracle Database.
  • Cloud services: Google Drive, OneDrive, and Dropbox for storage and collaboration.
  • Cybersecurity tools: Antivirus software, firewalls, and multi-factor authentication.

pages.title: Five Accounting-Specific IT Tools
pages.content:
Accounting tools serve different needs, from spreadsheet analysis to integrated enterprise operations.

ToolPrimary use
Microsoft ExcelFinancial analysis, budgeting, forecasting, and financial statements
QuickBooksBookkeeping, payroll, invoicing, and expense tracking for small and medium businesses
SAPEnterprise accounting integrated with finance, human resources, and supply chain operations
XeroCloud-based invoicing, bank reconciliation, and expense management
FreshBooksInvoicing, expense tracking, and reporting for small businesses and freelancers

pages.title: Lesson Summary
pages.content:
Information technology brings together hardware, software, data, people, processes, and networks. Businesses use these components to automate work, communicate, manage information, support decisions, compete, and protect data.

  • IT supports the complete accounting cycle, from recording transactions to reporting and compliance.
  • General business tools support documents, communication, databases, cloud collaboration, and security.
  • Excel, QuickBooks, SAP, Xero, and FreshBooks address different accounting needs.
  • The right tool depends on the task, organization size, workflow, and control requirements.
